messages:
secops: :rotating_light: Alert — a developer reported that a personal laptop backup (Google Drive) inadvertently contained a service credentials file with PROD DB connection strings. Treat as high priority and assume the credentials are compromised.

hana (eng): Confirmed. I was doing a one-off migration test and my backup agent picked up ~/projects/redwood/.env.prod and uploaded it to my personal Drive. I removed the file from Drive at 12:40 UTC after realizing but it may have been synced earlier.

secops: Thanks for reporting. For now assume any plaintext credentials in that file are compromised. We need immediate containment and rotations where appropriate.

max (infra): Can you paste the exact env keys (redacted) or the variable names so we can scope rotations? Also which DB cluster and user are referenced?

hana (eng): Variables: DATABASE_URL, REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON. DB user: app_migrator@redwood-prod-cluster. I redacted the values in the local copy before deleting, but the Drive revision may have the original.

sam (oncall): Quick detection commands for teams: search for copies of .env.prod or prod-like env files across home dirs and common backup locations. Also check SSO and Drive audit logs for external downloads.

```
# find prod env files in default dev paths
rg --hidden --no-ignore "DATABASE_URL|REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON" ~/ -S || true
# list recent Drive file activity (Gsuite admin)
gsutil ls -l gs://redwood-audit/drive-activity/ | tail -n 50
# find references in recent backup archives
find /backups -type f -name "*.tar.gz" -exec sh -c 'tar -xOzf "$0" .env.prod 2>/dev/null | rg "DATABASE_URL|REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON" -n || true' {} \;
```

oliver (support): We also saw a support case where a user attached a tarball named backup-2026-03-24.tar.gz. I'll check uploads in the last 48h against our ticket tracker.

legal-bot: Legal: if external exposure occurred (download by someone outside redwood.com), preserve logs and do not send external notifications without Legal approval. We may need coordinated disclosure if partner data is involved.

secops: Action items (company-wide):
- Immediate: Rotate DB user app_migrator credentials and revoke any active DB sessions.
- Rotate: Replace any service-account JSONs referenced in the file; issue new keys and migrate services to short-lived tokens.
- Audit: Search for copies of .env.prod and similar files across developer home dirs, CI runners, and backup repos (1 week retention min).
- Containment: Ask Hana to provide the Drive file id and any access logs; infra will request Drive audit from GSuite admin.
- Policy: Personal cloud backups that may contain company secrets are banned. We will publish an immediate guidance doc and enable DLP rules to detect uploads with production secrets.
- Postmortem: Capture root cause and follow-up automation to block uploads of prod secrets from known endpoints.

max (infra): Starting DB rotation now for app_migrator on redwood-prod-cluster. Will rotate creds and drop existing sessions; will post rotated key id. Also initiating a search across known backup buckets and home directories.

hana (eng): Drive file id: 1a2B3cDriveFileExample. I contacted Google and requested audit logs; I'll DM secops the owner email and timestamps.

sam (oncall): Examples for rotation commands (postgres):
```
# revoke connections and reset password for DB user
psql -h prod-db.redwood.internal -U admin -c "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename='app_migrator';"
psql -h prod-db.redwood.internal -U admin -c "ALTER ROLE app_migrator WITH PASSWORD 'NEW_STRONG_PASS';"
```

secops: Deadline: contain + rotations + initial audit results within 48 hours. We will treat any credentials found in Drive as compromised even if deleted. If you find evidence of access from external non-whitelisted IPs, escalate to Legal and SecOps.

oliver (support): My scan of last 48h support attachments found one user-submitted archive containing a file named env.prod.sample — no real secrets, but flagging potential pattern.

max (infra): Rotation complete for infra-managed DB credentials. Posted ticket SEC-2429999001 with changed credential ids and rotated service-account fingerprints.

legal-bot: Received Drive audit request. If Google confirms third-party access, Legal will advise on disclosure. Keep all copies and DO NOT share the original file outside secops/legal.

hana (eng): I will open MR to add a project-level .backupignore to prevent backing up files matching *.prod, .env*, and service-account*.json, and add a pre-commit hook and CI check. Pushing MR in ~2h.

sam (oncall): Full-hunt across developer home dirs and backups is running; will post high-priority hits to SEC-2429999001.

secops: New policy immediate enforcement: until DLP rules roll out, devs must disable personal cloud sync for any directory containing repositories or config files. We'll publish exact steps and an FAQ within 24h. Reopen this thread for status updates.
